title: Whittle a wedge-shaped end on a wooden stick
instruction: Whittle a 45 mm bevel on the end of the stick, leaving a blunt 2 mm thick tip. Put the intact stick and knife down in the tray.
context: Supporting a wooden blank while taking controlled shavings is a familiar craft skill. The blade must follow the grain away from the supporting hand.
setup: Development: 12 x 12 x 180 mm basswood stock, carving knife, chip tray. Exact fixed layout in geometry.py.
scoring: Intact stick required. Final tip thickness at most 10 mm: 0.25; at most 6 mm: 0.5; a complete 45 mm bevel ending at 2 mm: 0.75; 1.0 when the finished stick and knife are released in the tray for two seconds.
fidelity: Five coarse removable shavings approximate wood cutting. The edge applies 4 N resistance with equal and opposite reaction; this is an uncalibrated approximation. No chip release without loaded edge travel. Deep cuts or broken grain bonds invalidate the trial. Fine grain, burrs and wood fibres are not simulated.
scores: Development only: not validated; do not submit.
